bug_semantics: The ::import-binfile RPC accepted an optional, caller-controlled file-id for an in-place v3 import but authorized only the separately supplied project-id. The overwrite branch fetched the target file by id alone, imported attacker-controlled content with the caller's project-id, and updated the file row by the supplied target id, so an authenticated user who could edit their own project could overwrite and re-parent a victim file without permission on that file. The advisory's WebSocket-subscription language describes a related authorization omission, but the named import-binfile flaw and the BIC/fix fields here trace the file takeover mechanism.
flaw_origin: 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f is the smallest commit that created the vulnerable import path end to end: it added optional :file-id to schema:import-binfile, destructured and copied it into ::bfc/file-id, added import-file-and-overwrite* with an id-only get-minimal-file lookup, and made save-file! update rather than insert while preserving the caller-supplied project-id. Its direct parent had neither the external file-id parameter nor the overwrite branch and only created new imported files.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names author Andrey Antukh <niwi@niwi.nz> and committer Andrey Antukh <niwi@niwi.nz>; after the headers it contains only the subject ':tada: Add inplace binfile import support' and no body, Co-Authored-By trailer, Generated-with trailer, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7ff3-w2cq-gmpq identifies CVE-2026-17613/GHSA-7ff3-w2cq-gmpq and the unchecked optional file-id; the linked technical advisory https://vokecyber.com/research/cve-2026-17613-penpot-cross-team-file-takeover describes the one-request overwrite/re-parent attack. BIC: first-party commit https://github.com/penpot/penpot/commit/37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f. `git log -L 124,161:backend/src/app/rpc/commands/binfile.clj 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f` and exact-string `git log --all --reverse -F -S'[:file-id {:optional true} ::sm/uuid]'` show that 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f first added the optional parameter and passed it into overwrite configuration in backend/src/app/rpc/commands/binfile.clj:124-161. The same BIC added the id-only target lookup and overwrite transaction in backend/src/app/binfile/v3.clj:912-935, imported the archive under the caller-supplied project at backend/src/app/binfile/v3.clj:710-765 (the project assignment is line 757), and updated the existing row by id in backend/src/app/binfile/common.clj:516-535/558-569. Direct-parent proof: `git grep` for the exact schema entry, `assoc ::bfc/file-id file-id`, and `import-file-and-overwrite` against fd62141c04817c2ae86d10ad41b130fe616cf789 over those two source files returned no matches; the BIC diff shows the parent accepted only project-id/version/file and followed the new-file import path. Version boundary: `git tag --contains 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f` starts with the 2.10.0 release family; 2.9.0 has neither vulnerable line, while first affected RC 2.10.0-RC1 (tag 2a2735cd67994857d1cbdfbff148c41220a53f1e, 2025-09-01) and first affected stable 2.10.0 (tag d4b7f231c7a8c0ea4abdd271f32531e8b5e792e0, 2025-09-29) contain the BIC. This repository history therefore does not support the research article's claimed 'v1.20 onward' product-version boundary. Fix: first-party issue https://github.com/penpot/penpot/issues/10993 and PR https://github.com/penpot/penpot/pull/10994 lead to direct patch https://github.com/penpot/penpot/commit/461227fe16c3c188c1c88eb401205578cdd72caf and merged develop fix https://github.com/penpot/penpot/commit/9242556da6b87d646d766385c24575cc71a1c6a5; both remove file-id handling and close the RPC schema. Neither fix is contained by any tag. First-party releases https://github.com/penpot/penpot/releases/tag/2.17.0 and https://github.com/penpot/penpot/releases/tag/2.17.2 remain vulnerable: `git grep` finds both vulnerable lines in 2.17.0, 2.17.1, 2.17.2, and 2.18.0-RC1, including 2.17.2 tag 1d2c37e52c733f74017d90b0fd1ae2d074a5c33d dated 2026-08-27. Thus source is fixed on develop after 9242556da6b87d646d766385c24575cc71a1c6a5, but there is no tagged fixed-version boundary in the clone as of 2026-08-28. AI check: `git cat-file -p 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f` produced the exact author, committer, parent, and subject stated in ai_marker and no trailers. direct_fix_sha aligned to the landed fix 9242556da6b87d646d766385c24575cc71a1c6a5 (reconciliation 2026-08-29): the previously named commit 461227fe16c3c188c1c88eb401205578cdd72caf is a sibling branch/backport commit, not an ancestor of the landed fix (merge-base verified).
reasoning: The causal unit is not the older generic import RPC: before fd62141c04817c2ae86d10ad41b130fe616cf789's child, imports targeted a project the caller was authorized to edit and created new files. Commit 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f simultaneously exposed an arbitrary existing file id and implemented the id-only overwrite path. Because the authorization call remained scoped to project-id, an attacker could pass their own authorized project plus a victim file id; the BIC then loaded that victim row by id, wrote attacker archive data, and persisted the attacker's project-id, causing both destruction and takeover. Exact -S and -L history identify this commit rather than a later refactor, release, or fix, and direct-parent tree search proves the vulnerable mechanism absent. Tag ancestry places the first affected stable release at 2.10.0 and confirms that the latest inspected stable 2.17.2 is still affected. The original remediation commit 461227fe16c3c188c1c88eb401205578cdd72caf was reproduced as 9242556da6b87d646d766385c24575cc71a1c6a5 on develop, removing the dangerous parameter/use and closing the schema, but no release tag contains either fix. Finally, attribution is decided only from the BIC's raw commit object: it is a human-authored/human-committed object with no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
